# Worker brief — global config system · pij-technological-egret
**From**: pij-instant-lynx (o-prime) · **Date**: 2026-08-26 · one bounded task

## The job

Build fs3's centralized GLOBAL configuration system. Jordan's scope ruling: **global only** — `~/.config/flowspace3/` — NO per-repo/per-folder overrides yet (keep the loader layered-shaped so overrides can slot in later without redesign). Design distilled from fs2 research (what to copy/drop is settled — do not re-litigate):

### Layers (precedence low→high)
1. serde defaults on the config types (every field has one where sensible)
2. `~/.config/flowspace3/config.toml` (`FS3_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the dir — existing daemon behaviour, keep it)
3. `FS3_*` env var overrides with `__` nesting (`FS3_DATABASE__URL`) — strings, coerced by serde; this is how containers/tests override without files

### Secrets
Separate chain, never in config.toml: process env, then `~/.config/flowspace3/secrets.env` loaded INTO env at startup (daemon + cli). Config files reference env-var NAMES (the `api_key_env` shape already normative in providers) — no `${VAR}` templating. Never log secret values (s001 redaction rules).

### Types & injection (the DI story — compile-time, no registry)
- Config TYPES live in `fs3-core` (pure — serde only, no IO); the LOADER (file read, env merge, secrets load) lives in `fs3-daemon` config module (existing split, tk-0009 ruling; extend, don't relocate).
- One root `Config` struct of typed sections: `daemon`, `database`, `embedder`, `summarizer`, `scan` (new — carries the scanner-policy knobs like min-size thresholds; coordinate shape with the scanner worker mollusk ONLY via me if a conflict appears, likely none — you define the section, it consumes later).

# Ruling — PR-workflow cutover (Jordan, 2026-08-26)

> **EXECUTED 2026-08-27**: v0.2.0 shipped, fleet drained and closed, CI trigger
> moved to `pull_request`-only (commit 69d06ca), Jordan protecting main. From
> this point the operating model below is CURRENT, not queued. Coder briefs
> must state: own worktree + branch, conventional commits, PR into main as the
> done-bar; direct pushes to main are no longer possible.
Once the current work drains and the v0.2.0 release is done: main gets BRANCH PROTECTION and all
work moves to PRs from then on. At that moment (one cutover, deliberate): CI trigger moves from
push-to-main to pull_request-only, the green check becomes a merge requirement, and the push
trigger is removed (ox holds the mechanical change; noted in docs/services/ci-release.md).
Until cutover, the push-to-main gate + commit-push-as-you-go ruling stand unchanged.

## Operating model after cutover (Jordan, 2026-08-26, verbatim intent)
Same briefing discipline as today, different substrate: each coder gets its OWN git worktree +
branch for its packet ("each one can have their own work tree"), works there exactly as briefed,
and opens a PR when ready — instead of everyone committing to main. O-prime coordinates the
merging back in and the releases; worktrees are tidied up when the packet is done. Consequences:
- The shared-index/swept-stage class of incident disappears (no shared working tree).
- Fences become worktree+branch scoped; the descriptive-fence + notify-only convergence rule
  (global invariant 11) governs cross-worktree synchronization.
- Commit-push-as-you-go survives as commit-push-to-your-branch-as-you-go; conventional commits
  stay binding (release-please reads them).
- Merge order and conflict resolution are o-prime's coordination duty; releases remain
  Jordan-worded.

kind: difficulty
    description: "AMENDS DL-063 with the second layer, found by pij-devoted-cattle and verified verbatim here. 'harness commit --help' says: 'message  the commit message (passed to git as one argument \u2014 never a shell)'. That sentence is TRUE of harness's internals and actively misleading about this failure, because the mangling happens in the CALLER's shell before harness is ever executed. So a careful person who stops to wonder whether their backticks are safe reads a line that talks them out of looking. Combined with the only runtime signal being a 'command not found' printed above a status:ok JSON, it is a two-layer trap: one layer hides the warning in noise, the other pre-emptively answers the question that would have caught it. Also verified: there is NO -F or stdin option \u2014 usage is 'harness commit [options] <message> [pathspecs...]' \u2014 so the message can only arrive through argv, which is to say through a shell."
    target: project
    severity: blocking
    workaround: "Single-quote the message, or heredoc it into a file and expand that. Verified mechanism: echo \"a `true` b\" -> 'a  b'; echo 'a `true` b' -> intact."
    suggested_encoding: "'harness commit -F <file>' or read the message from stdin, which removes the shell from the path entirely rather than trying to detect damage after the fact \u2014 harness takes the message as argv and structurally cannot see what was typed, so detection is not available to it. AND FIX THE HELP LINE: it should say the message is passed to git unshelled BUT that the caller's own shell has already expanded it, naming backticks and $( ) explicitly. A true sentence that misdirects is worse than no sentence. Second-order note for the retro: cattle's six commits were undamaged only because they write identifiers bare in commit prose and reserve backticks for Markdown \u2014 a style habit, not knowledge. That is the cp-vs-mv shape twice in one day: which character our fingers reach for decided whether history was corrupted, and neither of …[fixture-truncated]
